title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
The relationship between film runtime and IMDb rating is shown in Figure Figure 1. This plot allows us to examine whether longer or shorter films tend to receive higher ratings.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb Rating")
plt.title("Film Runtime vs. IMDb Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtime versus IMDb rating






Mean IMDb Rating by Decade

films["decade"] = films["year"] // 10 * 10

title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page examines the relationship between a film’s budget and its worldwide revenue. Figure Figure 1 shows whether films with larger budgets tend to generate higher worldwide revenues.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (USD millions)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue (USD millions)")
plt.title("Film Budget vs. Worldwide Revenue")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film budget versus worldwide revenue

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue (USD millions)")
plt.title("James Bond Worldwide Revenue Over Time")
plt.show()








The first James Bond film in this dataset was released in { int(bond["year"].min()) }, and the last was released in { int(bond["year"].max()) }.

title: Box Office Numbers
text:
This website analyzes a dataset of 104 films from 1980 to 2025. The dataset includes film titles, release years, franchises, approximate budgets and worldwide revenues in millions of dollars, runtimes, and IMDb ratings.
The analysis explores the relationship between budget and revenue, runtime and ratings, and the revenue history of James Bond films.
